title.zh: 动作电位 · 全或无的神经脉冲
title.en: The action potential · an all-or-none nerve pulse

description.zh: 刺激把膜电位推过阈值，Na⁺ 通道成片打开、Na⁺ 涌入让电位冲到正值，随后 Na⁺ 通道失活、K⁺ 外流又把它拉回来甚至略低于静息；刺激再强，尖峰也不会更高，只会发得更频繁，而不应期给频率设了上限。
description.en: Once a stimulus pushes the membrane past threshold, Na⁺ channels open en masse and the inrush drives the voltage positive; then Na⁺ channels inactivate and K⁺ flows out, pulling it back, even slightly below rest; a stronger stimulus does not make a taller spike, only more frequent ones, and the refractory period caps the rate.

en: does a stronger stimulus give a bigger spike

reason.zh: 每个尖峰都从静息电位起跳、最后落回它附近；阈值也是相对静息电位而言，要推高十几毫伏才会触发。
reason.en: Every spike takes off from the resting potential and falls back near it; the threshold, too, is measured from rest — the voltage has to be pushed up by a dozen or so millivolts to trigger it.

label.en: Positive feedback in the Na⁺ channels

reason.zh: 电位一升，更多电压门控 Na⁺ 通道打开，Na⁺ 进得更多、电位升得更快——这是一条正反馈，所以过了阈值就停不下来，只能冲到顶，这正是“全或无”的来源。
reason.en: A rise in voltage opens more voltage-gated Na⁺ channels, letting in more Na⁺ and raising the voltage faster — positive feedback, which is why once past threshold the spike cannot stop halfway: the origin of “all-or-none”.
